name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,216

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sometime before five, at last landing place, but missing a passing procession

indicators.note: before tells us the first piece is placed ahead of what follows it
at last points to the final letter only of the word just given
missing means the word that follows must be left out of the piece

blocks.note: ex- means former, one-time
the last letter of five
a quay is a landing place for boats
the letter taken out of the landing place

explanation.surface: A boat comes in to its berth just before five o'clock, too late to watch a procession going by.
explanation.walkthrough: QUAY without its A gives QUY, so the answer is EX + E + QUY.
explanation.definitionFit: An exequy is a funeral rite, and a funeral cortege is a procession for someone who has passed away.

clue.text: Result of poet from the past, maybe, heading off west

definitions.note: a verb: to result, in the poet's (Spenser's) spelling

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away from the word before it

blocks.note: the past is an example of a grammatical tense
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A historian wonders what an old poet's work led to as it travelled westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the past, maybe' is a definition by example: the past is one tense. Lose its T to get ENSE, then add W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensew is Spenser's archaic spelling of ensue, meaning to follow on as a consequence.

clue.text: Mysterious Vern comes, not married, with ring on the other hand

indicators.note: not tells us the following abbreviation is to be removed
something mysterious is obscure and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for married, removed here
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man called Vern turns up single and wearing a ring, which is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: COMES loses its M to leave COES; with VERN that is rearranged, then the ring O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: E converso is a Latin phrase meaning conversely, used just as one says on the contrary or alternatively.

clue.text: US chemist recalled lawyer undertaking cases

indicators.note: cases means the words before it hold the answer inside them like a container
recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An American scientist remembers a lawyer who took on legal work for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Read lawYER Undertaking backwards to find UREY.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Urey was an American chemist who won the Nobel Prize for discovering deuterium.

clue.text: Stone fired over head of Zambian soldier once

indicators.note: head of means take only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
fired over again means set alight a second time
the opening letter of Zambian

explanation.surface: A stone is thrown across at a Zambian leader, perhaps by a soldier from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired over' looks like a missile flying overhead, but it means fired again.
explanation.definitionFit: A strelitz was a member of the old Muscovite guard of foot soldiers, disbanded by Peter the Great.

clue.text: Old Babylonian emperor cut half every six months?

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened by trimming its tail letter
half means only the first half of the word is kept, the rest discarded

blocks.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor
biannual means occurring twice a year

explanation.surface: An ancient king of Babylon gets a trim, but only halfway, twice a year.
explanation.walkthrough: TSAR loses its last letter to give TSA; BIANNUAL keeps its first four letters, BIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsabian is a variant of Sabian, a member of an ancient star-worshipping sect of Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Urchins from the city welcome? Not a clue!

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
hi is a greeting
having not a clue means having no idea

explanation.surface: Street kids from town are greeted with a shrug of total ignorance.
explanation.walkthrough: Urchins here are sea urchins, not ragamuffins; EC is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinoidea is the zoological class containing the sea urchins and sand dollars.

clue.text: Desert plant — about to leave for one gets stress

indicators.note: to leave for means one piece departs and another takes its place

blocks.note: a cactus grows in the desert
ca, short for circa, means about
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cactus in the desert is strained when someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: In CACTUS the CA is swapped for I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is the rhythmical or metrical accent on a syllable in verse.

clue.text: These merged with zinc to form rocky deposit

indicators.note: merged suggests things blended together so their letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geology lesson: these minerals combined with zinc to make a stony layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zechstein is a European rock series of Upper Permian strata, rich in salt and limestone deposits.

clue.text: Cape, behold, turned up with sash for primates

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is written from the bottom upward

blocks.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
lo means look, behold
an obi is a Japanese sash

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a cape and sash, dressed up as an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Colobi is a plural of colobus, an African monkey, so the word names a group of primates.

clue.text: Victorian rest homes, condemned, accepting fine

indicators.note: condemned buildings are wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: Nineteenth-century rest homes are condemned but somehow get a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian means from the Australian state of Victoria, not the era; smoke-ho is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoko or smoke-ho is the Australian and New Zealand term for a short break from work.

clue.text: Dark area still keeps burning

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a is an abbreviation for area
a still photograph is a pic
something burning is hot

explanation.surface: A dark patch is still smouldering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is a noun, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphotic describes zones, especially deep ocean, that receive no sunlight and so are lightless.

clue.text: Marry old Victor’s double in start of wish for long life?

indicators.note: in start of means it is placed in the opening position, replacing what was there

blocks.note: W was once written as two Vs, and Victor is V in the radio alphabet
vive, as in vive le roi, means long live

explanation.surface: An old man called Victor appears twice in a wish for a long life.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening V of VIVE is swapped for W, a doubled V.
explanation.definitionFit: To wive is an old verb meaning to take a woman as wife, that is to wed.

clue.text: Ideas people mad to insist on

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Creative types are crazy about insisting on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Notionists are people who hold fanciful notions, theorists given to speculative thinking.

clue.text: Clash arising with this country hotel about carriage for young head of state

indicators.note: in a down entry, arising means going upward, so the word reads from the bottom
about here places the country and hotel beside, on the subject of, the carriage that precedes them

blocks.note: to jar is to clash
a pram carries a baby
the setter writes from the United Kingdom
Hotel is H in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in a country hotel over a pram belonging to a youthful ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young head of state' reads as one phrase, but young belongs to the pram; the definition is just head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajpramukh was the governor of certain Indian states formed from former princely states after independence.

clue.text: Leaves arrangement of rave to inn, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, here a new order of letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party crowd moves from a rave to a pub, and the order they leave in is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing; it is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernation is the botanical term for how young foliage is folded inside the bud.

clue.text: See higher purpose initially in a stratagem idiot picked up

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of the word before
in means placed inside, so that letter sits within the next word
in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so everything is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
a ruse is a trick or stratagem
first letter of purpose
div is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot hatches a cunning plan with a higher purpose in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Div is British slang for a fool. In a down clue the whole string is built first and then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Vide supra is a Latin note in texts directing the reader to look at an earlier passage above.

clue.text: No time for wee hint!

indicators.note: No signals the item named next is to be taken away

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
tinkle is a childish word for a wee, urination

explanation.surface: A hurried hint that there is no time for a toilet break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like Scottish small, but it is the noun; TINKLE loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkle is a dialect verb meaning to hint at, from the same root as inkling, a slight suggestion.

clue.text: Scottish writer’s endless furious interrupting briefly lamented

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut from the word that follows
interrupting means breaking into the middle of another word
briefly means made shorter by dropping the last letter

blocks.note: livid means furious
to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: A Scottish author is furious at being cut short by mourners.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer means the implement, not an author; to keen is to wail over the dead, an Irish and Scottish custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelivine is a Scots word for a lead pencil, an implement used for writing.

clue.text: Pants with waistband finally going left to sag

indicators.note: finally means take only the last letter of the word before
going left means travelling right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, poor
last letter of waistband

explanation.surface: Trousers whose elastic has given up start to slip down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear, but it is the British adjective for bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to hang down limply, the same as to sag.

clue.text: Driver’s warning about salt water submerging live vegetable plant

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the rest
submerging means putting underneath, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a driver sounds the horn as a warning
the sea is salt water
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A motorist hoots at a sea washing over a living vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the verb for living goes inside the water, and that goes inside the warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse bean is a variety of broad bean grown as fodder, a leguminous crop.

clue.text: Cheered as Zulu — a boxing unknown — shaded rounds

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the pair holds the next letter between them
rounds means goes round, so the last word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: hued means coloured or shaded
Zulu is Z in the radio alphabet
z is a mathematical unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd applauds as a Zulu boxer, an unknown, edges the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zulu — a' is read as one pair of letters that boxes the unknown; the shaded word then goes round all three.
explanation.definitionFit: To huzza is to shout hurrah, so huzzaed means shouted in acclaim.

clue.text: Aussie creature going over stone grating in Perth

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means sitting above, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: roo is Australian for kangaroo
the stone of a fruit is its pit

explanation.surface: A kangaroo hops over a stone drain cover in Perth, Western Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish town, so the definition is a Scots word, not an Australian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Roopit is Scots for hoarse, and a hoarse voice sounds harsh and rasping.

clue.text: Polish ready, nearly, to go on blemish covering hard, wide glass decoration

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to go on means to be placed after what comes next
covering means wrapping around, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: a scar is a blemish
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
w is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
ready is slang for cash, and the zloty is Polish currency

explanation.surface: Someone buffs a glass ornament until it is almost done, hiding a hard, wide flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb, but it is the nationality; ZLOTY loses its Y. A wide is a ball bowled out of reach in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwarzlot is black enamel painting used to decorate German and Bohemian glass and porcelain.

clue.text: Charmed by opening note

indicators.note: opening means prising apart, so the word splits to take another inside

blocks.note: to note is to heed
x means by, as in 3 x 4 dimensions

explanation.surface: Someone is enchanted by the first note of a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes into the middle of HEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexed means put under a spell, bewitched, just as charmed can mean enchanted by magic.

clue.text: Take too much out of alkaline element in water parsnips

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the first piece leaves the second

blocks.note: to OD is to overdose
sodium is an alkali metal

explanation.surface: Water parsnips should not contain too much of an alkaline element.
explanation.walkthrough: SODIUM loses OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sium is the botanical genus of umbelliferous marsh plants commonly called water parsnips.

clue.text: Some salmon beginning to mate like place across pond

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: first letter of mate
as means like
across the pond, from Britain, is America

explanation.surface: Salmon start to mate in a spot just like one across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some salmon' looks like a hidden-word signal but is the plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The masu is a Pacific salmon of Japan, so masus are several of those fish.

clue.text: Advise against releasing our age for the record

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so those words are taken away

blocks.note: to discourage is to advise against
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A spokesperson declines, on the record, to give anyone's age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the record' reads as an idiom, but the record is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or other recorded music medium.

clue.text: Pennies, gold, returning sailor put about cross one’s palm

indicators.note: put about means placed around, so the first word encloses the next
returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for pence
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
x is a cross
I is the Roman numeral one
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A fortune teller asks a returning sailor to cross her palm with pennies and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold goes round the cross and the one; 'cross one's palm' is an idiom for paying a fortune teller, but palm is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The paxiuba is a tall South American stilt-rooted palm tree, used for building and spears.

clue.text: African people’s life to be digested by one another time

indicators.note: to be digested by means to be swallowed, taken inside the other pieces

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bis means twice, a call for a repeat
bio is short for biography, a life story

explanation.surface: A tribe's way of life is absorbed by outsiders time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Bis, Latin for twice, is a call for an encore; the one sits in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibibio are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so Ibibios are members of that nation.

clue.text: Compound of molten lead — one doctor would turn to

indicators.note: molten metal loses its shape, so the letters are recast in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
in Stevenson's tale Dr Jekyll turns into Mr Hyde

explanation.surface: A chemist's compound of melted metal that a doctor might take up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the verb, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldehyde is an organic chemical compound containing a CHO group, such as formaldehyde.

clue.text: Navy game in which dupe’s first to get to the end

indicators.text: first to get to the end
indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front to the back of the word

blocks.note: a sucker is someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A naval game in which the fool who moves first races to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Uckers is a board game like ludo, traditionally played in the Royal Navy.
